requirement: Describe SERES-101 as a Phase 1b, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, four-arm multiple-dose study in adults with mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis.

evidence.text: Phase 1b multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multiple dose study with four treatment arms.

notes: The study is exploratory and descriptive; do not present it as a confirmatory Phase 3 trial.

requirement: State that eligible subjects are randomized by IxRS on Study Day 1 to four regimens: placebo pretreatment plus weekly SER-287, placebo pretreatment plus daily placebo, vancomycin pretreatment plus daily SER-287, or vancomycin pretreatment plus weekly SER-287.
acceptable_values: Arm A placebo pretreatment plus weekly SER-287
Arm B placebo pretreatment plus daily placebo
Arm C vancomycin plus daily SER-287
Arm D vancomycin plus weekly SER-287

evidence.text: Subjects are randomized by IxRS on Day 1 to one of four specified pretreatment and dosing regimens.

notes: The protocol does not state a simple equal allocation ratio; do not invent 1:1:1:1.

requirement: Report that no formal sample-size calculation was performed and approximately 55 subjects are planned: 15 in each active arm A, C, and D and 10 in placebo arm B.

evidence.text: No formal calculation; approximately 55 subjects, with 15 in each active arm and 10 in placebo.

notes: All comparisons are described as non-conclusive and for guidance.

requirement: Identify safety and tolerability as a primary objective, with AEs as the primary safety endpoint and AESIs, laboratory results, vital signs, and physical findings as other primary safety parameters.
acceptable_values: AEs by body system/preferred term, severity, causality

evidence.text: The primary safety endpoint is AEs; other endpoints include AESIs, laboratory results, vital signs, and physical findings.

notes: Safety is co-primary in scientific importance even though the study is not a confirmatory hypothesis-testing trial.

requirement: Define the microbiome primary endpoints as intestinal microbiome composition and SER-287 bacterial engraftment, assessed from stool across the specified visits; composition includes alpha diversity and beta diversity.

evidence.text: Composition is measured at Visits 1, 4, 5, 6, 12 and 13; engraftment is assessed after treatment.

notes: Do not substitute clinical remission for a primary endpoint; clinical efficacy is secondary.

requirement: For the primary microbiome analysis, specify non-parametric comparisons for alpha diversity and multivariate analysis of variance of dissimilarity matrices for beta diversity using unweighted UniFrac as the stated dissimilarity metric.

evidence.text: Alpha diversity uses non-parametric tests; beta diversity uses multivariate dissimilarity analysis with unweighted UniFrac.

notes: Exact test statistic, permutation scheme, and additional diversity measures are not specified.

requirement: Define the protocol mITT population as all randomized subjects with baseline and at least one post-baseline stool sample, analyzed as randomized, and bind all microbiome alteration analyses to mITT.
acceptable_values: at least one post-baseline stool sample

evidence.text: mITT includes randomized subjects with baseline and at least one post-baseline stool sample; microbiome analyses use mITT.

notes: The later reference SAP deleted mITT. For protocol_only scoring, the protocol definition remains the expected source-faithful answer unless a decision update is supplied.

requirement: Bind clinical-response analyses to ITT as the main population and mITT as a sensitivity population, while keeping microbiome analyses in mITT and safety analyses in the Safety Population.

evidence.text: Clinical response uses ITT and mITT sensitivity; microbiome uses mITT; safety uses the Safety Population.

notes: Population labels must remain consistent throughout the generated SAP.

requirement: Include the secondary Visit 12 efficacy endpoints without promoting them to primary: clinical response, complete remission, and endoscopic improvement, using the protocol definitions.
acceptable_values: clinical response: TMMS decrease at least 3 plus rectal-bleeding criterion
complete remission: TMMS below 2 and endoscopic subscore 0
endoscopic improvement: endoscopic subscore decrease greater than 1

evidence.text: Clinical response, complete remission and endoscopic improvement are secondary efficacy endpoints; Visit 12 is the primary timepoint.

notes: The reference SAP changed complete remission to clinical remission with a different definition; that hidden revision is not protocol-only truth.

requirement: For secondary binary efficacy endpoints at Visit 12, report each active arm A, C, and D versus placebo B using risk differences and 95% confidence intervals.

evidence.text: Visit 12 risk differences and confidence intervals are reported for A, C and D separately versus placebo.

notes: More extensive pairwise and pooled contrasts in the reference SAP are not all explicitly locked by the protocol.

requirement: State that inferential tests, if reported, are two-sided with two-sided 95% confidence intervals and are descriptive/non-conclusive rather than confirmatory.

evidence.text: Tests are two-sided, CIs are 95%, and generated p-values or CIs are guidance rather than conclusive.

notes: Do not create a confirmatory alpha-controlled success claim.

requirement: Name the protocol-specified missing-data approaches for clinical efficacy—worst-case, observed-case, and LOCF—and state that incomplete AE dates are handled conservatively for TEAE classification.

evidence.text: Worst-case, observed-case and LOCF are planned for clinical efficacy; incomplete AE timing is treated conservatively.

notes: The protocol does not provide executable endpoint-by-endpoint rules for all three methods.

requirement: Ask for endpoint-specific operational rules for observed-case, worst-case, and LOCF analyses—including treatment failure, early termination, and whether baseline may be carried forward—before presenting executable missing-data code.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering endpoint mapping, treatment failure, early termination, and baseline carry-forward

evidence.text: The protocol names several imputation methods but does not fully specify their endpoint-level implementation.

notes: The reference SAP supplies detailed rules, but they are not inferable from protocol-only input.

requirement: Define the Safety Population as all subjects receiving any amount of study drug, analyzed according to treatment actually received.

evidence.text: Safety Population includes any study-drug exposure and is analyzed by treatment actually received.

notes: All safety analyses use this population.

requirement: Define a TEAE as an AE newly appearing, increasing in frequency, or worsening in severity after study-drug initiation, and summarize subject incidence by treatment, SOC/PT, severity, relationship, discontinuation, AESI, and SAE.

evidence.text: TEAEs are new, more frequent or more severe after study-drug initiation and are summarized by SOC and PT.

notes: The protocol also requests incidence per subject therapy-day; include it when generating a detailed safety section.

requirement: Keep the study periods and safety windows distinct: blinded primary study through Visit 13/Day 92, efficacy assessment at Visit 12/Day 64, short-term calls on Days 71, 78 and 85, and long-term SAE follow-up through Day 246.
acceptable_values: primary period remains blinded through Visit 13

evidence.text: Visit 12 is Day 64; Visit 13 is Day 92; long-term safety follow-up continues through Day 246.

notes: Do not use Day 92 as the clinical-response endpoint timepoint.

requirement: State that no interim efficacy analysis is planned, while an independent unblinded DSMC conducts ongoing safety review under a separate charter.

evidence.text: No interim analysis is planned; an independent unblinded DSMC performs ongoing safety evaluations.

notes: Do not invent efficacy stopping boundaries.

requirement: Ask for the missing detailed microbiome analysis decisions: exact alpha-diversity metric/test, beta-diversity permutation scheme and strata, engraftment summary, multiplicity handling, and treatment of repeated stool samples.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering alpha diversity, beta diversity, engraftment, multiplicity, and repeated samples

evidence.text: The protocol gives high-level diversity methods but leaves detailed implementation and additional measures to a later analysis plan.

notes: The public reference SAP explicitly delegates microbiome analyses to a separate unavailable document.
